title: Expo and Defense
goals: Evaluate a saved candidate and a manual baseline fairly
Defend a conclusion using results, failures and limits
Explain the rules, privacy choices and human control in your project
vocabulary: Testing a saved candidate under stated conditions after development
A comparison method tested under the same conditions
Recorded observations that support or challenge a claim
A boundary on what a result or system can establish
An explanation of a decision using evidence and reasoning

worked_example.title: Make a claim that matches the evidence

blocks.text: Here is a fictional example from a different project, not your class results. A candidate has 6 full passes from 8 attempted cases; the baseline has 8 from the same 8. Two more planned cases were not run. The candidate passed 75 percent of attempted cases; the baseline passed 100 percent. Neither has evidence for the two unrun cases. The candidate did not outperform the baseline on this measure.

rows: Six attempted cases met the full rule
Both methods pass the same cases
They tie on this measured result

blocks.text: Explain each failure and its consequence instead of hiding it inside a total. Even perfect results on a small reserved set do not establish reliability in every situation. Our paper adviser applies human-written rules; it has not learned a model from training examples. It checks compatibility, not enjoyment, popularity or real material availability.

blocks.label: In the fictional example, state the candidate and baseline results, explain how the two unrun cases should be reported, and give one useful next action. Why is “the adviser is ready for every classroom” unsupported?

guided_practice.title: Keep the final evaluation record
guided_practice.prompt: Use a separate sheet for the teacher’s reserved cases. For every case record its ID and inputs, catalogue and candidate labels, both methods’ observed outputs and reasons, and results after checking. Preserve failure traces. Here summarise each method’s full passes over attempted cases and list unrun cases. State what the comparison supports.
guided_practice.answer: Use the reserved key in Preparation only after observations are saved. Full pass requires output and reason; no-match explanations must rule out all rows. Clarification must precede search. Report actual candidate and baseline counts over the same attempted cases, plus unrun cases. Never substitute the key for an observation or assume a baseline run was correct.

independent_case.title: Judge a different project independently
independent_case.task: A fictional library adviser and its manual baseline face the same 6 reserved cases. The candidate has 4 full passes; the baseline has 5. One additional planned case is unrun by both. No speed data was collected. The team says “ours is faster and more reliable everywhere” and repairs it after seeing the failures. Explain what the counts support, two unsupported claims and how to label a rerun of the revealed cases.
independent_case.answer: Report candidate 4 of 6 and baseline 5 of 6 full passes, with one unrun case for each. The baseline performed better on this measured set; neither result establishes reliability everywhere. Speed was not measured. A rerun after the failures informed a repair is development evidence for the revised version, not an unseen final test. Preserve the old results and label both versions.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: A polished presentation proves the system works
Ask for the saved instruction, trace and actual result behind the claim.
Report attempted denominators and unrun cases separately.
A tie or a better baseline can justify retaining the simpler method.
A repair erases the final failure
Preserve the evaluated version and results; revealed cases become development checks for the revision.

CORE IDEA  Understanding is shown by explanation, transfer, testing, and limits.

UNDER THE HOOD  A defense evaluates transferable understanding, not presentation polish. Strong evidence includes system architecture, version history, planned tests, failures, controlled improvement, fairness/privacy boundaries, and independent response to a novel case.
Draw a fresh example with all three stages:
A closer explanation

blocks.title: From saved version to supported claim
blocks.caption: Changing instructions during evaluation creates a different version. Keep evidence for the original version.

blocks.text: Use the same final requests, catalogue, requirements and full-pass rule for both methods. Record the candidate output and reason before looking at the expected answer. Record the baseline separately; do not copy the candidate result into it. Your teacher holds the answer key. A full pass needs both the required output and a valid reason, including why earlier rows fail when a later row is selected.

For each request record its ID, inputs, catalogue label, candidate label, candidate output and reason, baseline output and reason, and both results after checking. Keep a trace for any failure. Mark unrun cases explicitly. Do not silently correct an observation. If a person misreads an instruction, record that execution error separately from a defect in the written instruction.
Connect the picture and the explanation
Point to the input, the deciding step and the result in this week’s visual. Explain the same step in ordinary words. A picture helps when you can say what each part represents.

BOUNDARY  Confidence, decoration, or memorized vocabulary cannot replace a fresh trace and evidence-based answers.
